claims.text: A thin Mo interlayer between W and CuCrZr improves interfacial bonding under fusion-reactor conditions.
A Mo interlayer mitigates the thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
A Mo interlayer acts as a diffusion barrier between W and CuCrZr.
A directly bonded W/CuCrZr interface suffers from high residual stresses.
A directly bonded W/CuCrZr interface suffers from undesirable interdiffusion.
The residual stresses at a direct W/CuCrZr interface arise from mismatched thermal-expansion coefficients.
A thin Mo layer can be deposited on one or both joining surfaces by magnetron sputtering and subsequently annealed at high temperature.
Fusion-reactor materials can experience extreme temperatures, stresses, and high heat fluxes.
The relevant operating conditions include cyclic thermal stresses.
Mo has thermal properties intermediate between those of W and CuCrZr.
Mo has chemical properties intermediate between those of W and CuCrZr.
Mo has an intermediate coefficient of thermal expansion that accommodates strain mismatch and reduces interfacial residual stress.
The Mo diffusion barrier suppresses harmful intermetallic-phase formation at the W/CuCrZr interface.
Relative to a direct W/CuCrZr join, the Mo interlayer produces a more stable and durable interface with better bonding integrity.
Relative to a direct W/CuCrZr join, the Mo interlayer improves resistance to degradation induced by thermal cycling.
The performance benefit depends on optimizing the Mo-layer thickness and thermal treatment.
Temperatures beyond Mo's stability range or non-optimized deposition conditions can undermine the interlayer's benefits.
